chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Fats Waller at the Apollo: Hammond organ, wine bottles and appetite
summary: The last time Jackson saw Fats was at the Apollo; Waller had a Hammond organ, gave every bandsman a bottle, and ate from serving dishes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But, just like we said about Fats, Fats could mix in anywhere --
Any place.
-- with anybody and he would bring happiness wherever he went, you know.
What a person.
And I used to go hear him every chance I got. The last time I heard him was in the Apollo Theater.

Hammond had just given him an organ. In fact, Hammond built a three manual organ for him in his house, that he had in his house out here. The top manual had a novochord and solo-vox accompaniment on it back there in those days.
Wow.

But he had this new, I think it was a new B-3 organ that Hammond -- and he told me to come back stage, and, you know, I went up to his room; you know, Fats always kept wine up there. He never would give you a drink out of his bottle.
He drank gin, wasn't it? Wasn't he a gin --
No, he was drinking wine then. They had taken him off of gin.
Oh, I see.
He was drinking wine then and he never would give you a drink out of his bottle. He'd pass you a whole bottle for yourself.
(Laughter.)
That's right. He never would give you a drink out of his bottle. He would give you a bottle. And everybody in his band, when they opened up, there was a bottle in front of their stand, --
Wow.
-- on the bandstand. A bottle for each
guy in the band.
He was some kind of cat.
What a beautiful person he was.
Yes.
And he ate. He was a big eater. His wife used to bring his dinner in a clothes basket. You know, one of those old-fashioned clothes baskets?
Right.
And not a plate for him to eat, but the food would all be in serving dishes and he would eat out of the serving dishes.
I see.

You see. And he'd never ask you to have a taste. He never asked you to have any of his food. And he'd laugh and talk, he'd laugh. Talking about him, oh, he was such a lovable guy. And that's the last I saw him was in the Apollo Theater and he told me to come on the other side of the stage, he wanted me to hear this organ because he knew I liked the organ, you know.
